kernel.governing_law: The cosmos operates through cycles of quiet return and patient accumulation: what is powerful begins as a buried tremor, grows through non-forcing obedience to natural timing, and is gathered inward as stored virtue — thunder hidden, thunder governed, heaven contained.
kernel.mutated_relation: What is powerful arrives as sudden, ungovernable rupture that neither waits, nor obeys, nor can be stored — the scale where containment fails and the tremor becomes the quake.

artifacts.enantiomorph:
100000
爆发 地雷爆发 坤上震下
爆发：势不可挡。烈焰吞天一瞬贯穿碾碎一切，万物俱震。反复其道，一击不返。无处可往。
译文：《爆发卦》象征爆发：势不可挡。烈焰从下面产生而一瞬贯穿碾碎一切，万物俱震。返回复归已无可能，一击不返。无处可往
象曰："雷裂地表，爆发；无主以正午烈日城门崩裂，众生奔逃，后不四方皆废。
译文：《象辞》说：《爆发卦》的卦象是震(雷)下坤(地)上，为雷裂地表、烈焰吞天之表象，因而象征爆发；无主之世在正午烈日这一刻城门崩裂，使众生奔逃，不外出经商、旅行，四方皆废
100111
狂肆 天雷狂肆 乾上震下
狂肆：无序无道，正道断绝。其匪正有眚，无处可往。
译文：《狂肆卦》象征狂肆：无序无道，正道断绝。然而，正道已断绝就会发生祸殃，因而也就无处可往了
象曰：天下雷行，物与狂肆；无主以时序崩溃万物自焚。
译文：《象辞》说：《狂肆卦》的卦象是震(雷)下乾(天)上，好比在天的下面有雷在运行之表象，象征着雷以全势毁弃万物，万物皆失其性；无主之世时序崩溃万物自焚
111001
大溃 山天大溃 艮上乾下
大溃：倾泻殆尽；无所守；无家可归凶，大川倒流。
译文：《大溃卦》象征倾泻殆尽：无所守；不要让疯先知穷困地居于家中自谋生计，而无家可归，这样便可以获得凶兆；大川倒流
象曰：山在天中碎裂，大溃；幸存者以忘却一切旧言旧行，以骨为薪。
译文：《象辞》说：《大溃卦》的卦象是乾(天)下艮(山)上，为山在天中碎裂之表象，象征倾泻殆尽；幸存者效法这一精神，应当忘却一切旧言旧行，以骨为薪
artifacts.enantiomorph_translation:
100000
Eruption, Earth-Thunder Eruption, Kun above Zhen below
Eruption: unstoppable. Wildfire devours the sky, piercing through in an instant, crushing all — the ten thousand things tremble together. The way of return is gone, one strike never returning. Nowhere to go.
Commentary: "Thunder splits the earth's surface" — Eruption; in the masterless world at the blazing noon sun the city gates collapse, all living things flee, and the four directions are laid to waste.
Commentary explained: The image of the Eruption hexagram is Zhen (thunder) below Kun (earth) above — thunder rending the earth's surface, wildfire devouring the sky — thus symbolizing eruption; in the masterless age, at the moment of the blazing noon sun, the city gates collapse, all living things flee, unable to travel or trade, the four directions all ruined.

100111
Frenzy, Heaven-Thunder Frenzy, Qian above Zhen below
Frenzy: without order, without dao; the true way is severed. Where the way is no longer upright, calamity arises — nowhere to go.
Commentary: Under heaven thunder moves, and all things are given over to frenzy; the masterless age, when the sequence of seasons collapses and the ten thousand things burn themselves.
Commentary explained: The image of the Frenzy hexagram is Zhen (thunder) below Qian (heaven) above — thunder moving beneath heaven — symbolizing that thunder with full force destroys and discards the ten thousand things, and all things lose their natures; in the masterless world, the order of seasons collapses and the ten thousand things immolate themselves.

111001
Great Collapse, Mountain-Heaven Great Collapse, Gen above Qian below
Great Collapse: poured out to the last drop; nothing to hold; homeless and ill-fated — the great river flows backward.
Commentary: The mountain shatters amid the sky — Great Collapse; the survivors forget all former words and former deeds, and burn bone for fuel.
Commentary explained: The image of the Great Collapse hexagram is Qian (heaven) below Gen (mountain) above — the mountain shattering in the midst of the sky — symbolizing everything poured out to exhaustion; the survivors, emulating this spirit, forget all old words and old deeds, and use bone as kindling.

independent.recovered_law: TEXT B systematically inverts the directional valence of every hexagram's core relation: what in TEXT A flows as gradual restoration, orderly restraint, and beneficial accumulation (复→return/renewal, 无妄→not acting recklessly, 大畜→great accumulation) becomes in TEXT B catastrophic eruption, total dissolution, and irreversible destruction (爆发→explosion, 狂肆→wild abandon, 大溃→great collapse). The governing agent (先王/君主) is replaced by absence of authority (无主/幸存者), and all outcomes flip from auspicious to calamitous.
independent.law_match_note: Both describe a shift toward ungovernable rupture and failure of containment, but the recovered claim specifies a systematic inversion of every hexagram's directional valence (restoration→destruction, authority→absence) — a broader structural inversion pattern that only partially overlaps the declared focus on scale/containment failure.
independent.terminal_note: The final hexagram (大溃) fully sustains the inverted relation—accumulation becomes collapse, the ruler becomes survivors, and virtuous cultivation becomes self-destruction—with no reversion to TEXT A's structure.
